title: Smart Thermostat Rebates in Kingston 2026: $125 Back
desc: Kingston smart thermostat rebate for 2026: $125 from Home Renovation Savings, Utilities Kingston as distributor, and the free Energy Affordability Program.
lead: Kingston has the second-highest renter share on our list, 44% of 57,835 households, so who holds the account and who owns the thermostat matters here.
cards_heading: What Ontario pays for a smart thermostat in Kingston
cards_intro: We re-read the three program pages on October 4, 2026. The rebate is province-wide, so the amount is the same in every city, and the page that matters is the one that says whether your home and heating qualify.

cards.title: Smart thermostat
cards.note: One rebate on an eligible smart thermostat, claimed with a code at checkout or with a receipt uploaded within 60 days of buying.

cards.title: Who is eligible
cards.amount: Gas heat or electric heat or cooling
cards.note: You must be an Enbridge Gas customer heating mainly with a gas furnace or boiler, or be on the Ontario grid and use electric heat or cooling, and live in a house, semi, row, townhome or mobile home on a permanent foundation.

cards.title: One per household, ever
cards.note: A smart thermostat rebate, discount or free device from Enbridge, Save on Energy or Home Renovation Savings in the past rules you out.

cards.title: Peak Perks
cards.note: A prepaid card for joining the summer demand response program with central air or a heat pump controlled by an eligible Wi-Fi thermostat.

cards.title: Energy Affordability Program
cards.note: Households under the income limits get a programmable or smart thermostat, depending on the home, with other upgrades at no charge.

cards.title: Cornwall excluded
cards.note: Cornwall Electric customers cannot join the rebate or Peak Perks.

after_cards: The rebate page states no end date, so confirm it is still open before you buy.
sections: 56% of Kingston households own and 44% rent. Only 63% live in a house type covered by the $125 rebate. For tenants, the useful steps are to find out whether the home qualifies, ask the landlord before replacing a thermostat and ask whether the unit stays when they move.

Utilities Kingston supplies electricity here. The Energy Affordability Program accepts renters who hold the utility account, and Kingston postal codes begin with K, which the program lists. If the electricity is included in the rent, the landlord holds the account, and the application should come from them.

The program pays for single detached, semi-detached, row, townhome and mobile homes on a permanent foundation. In Kingston about 63% of 57,835 households live in one of those. If yours is an apartment or a duplex unit, this rebate is not written for you, and the Energy Affordability Program is the route to ask about.

The Energy Affordability Program covers postal codes beginning K, L, M, N and P, which includes Kingston. Income limits for comprehensive support run from $48,220 for one person to $96,439 for four and $107,823 for five or more. Owners and renters who hold the utility account can apply, by phone at 1-844-770-3148 or online. The program says it is fully funded and accepting applications.

The most common reason for a refusal is an earlier offer. If you ever received a thermostat, a discount or a rebate on one from Enbridge Gas, Save on Energy or Home Renovation Savings, the program treats this as a second claim. If you are not sure, look for old emails or ask the program before you buy.
claim_steps: Check that your home type, heating and cooling match the eligibility card, and that you have not had a thermostat offer before.
Pick one of the listed models from ecobee, Google Nest, Honeywell Home, Copeland Sensi, Mysa or Sinopé.
Get a code from the program page and use it at checkout, or buy first and upload the receipt within 60 days.
If you have central air, enroll the same thermostat in Peak Perks. Utilities Kingston is your local distributor, but Peak Perks is run by Save on Energy.
If your household income is under the program limits, call 1-844-770-3148 before buying, since a free thermostat may be available.
faq: Can a Kingston renter get a free thermostat?
Yes, if they hold the utility account and their income is under the limit, or they receive a listed support such as ODSP or Ontario Works.
Does Utilities Kingston give a rebate?
We did not find one on the pages we read.
Does the student housing near the university qualify?
Only if it is an eligible home type, and the landlord should agree.
What counts as a previous offer?
Any smart thermostat rebate, discount or device from Enbridge Gas, Save on Energy or Home Renovation Savings.
